note: Frozen eval subset: queries never feed the fine-tune distribution.

queries.query: Ouspensky's argument that a flat creature confined to a plane would experience our third dimension as time, treating everything off its plane as past or future rather than as elsewhere
queries.note: The plane-being analogy chapters; 'section', 'angle', 'third perpendicular', 'spiral and film' paraphrased away; Ouspensky kept as the author's name.

queries.query: the claim that a horse or cat perceives no depth at all, reading solids as shifting flat appearances, so an animal's world has one dimension fewer than a man's
queries.note: The animal-perception chapter; 'series of complicated moving surfaces', 'angles and curves as motion' paraphrased into shifting flat appearances.

queries.query: the analysis of the present moment as nothing but a boundary where what has not yet arrived crosses into what no longer exists, hinting that time is really an unperceived dimension of space
queries.note: 'The moment of transition of a phenomenon from one non-existence into another non-existence' recast; 'motion in space and motion in time' dropped.

queries.query: why Ouspensky calls love a cosmic force in which individual human beings are mere incidents, its enormous surplus beyond what reproduction needs destined for another kind of creation
queries.note: The occultism-and-love chapter; 'cosmic phenomenon in which men, humanity, are merely accidents', 'creation of the future by begetting' paraphrased.

queries.query: is the universe one eternal being rather than an endless becoming
queries.note: Language pictures a dual, becoming universe that is really one and being; the eternal-now question is answered across traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: do stones, trees, and mountains possess souls or an inner life of their own
queries.note: The animated-nature chapter and the voices of stones; panpsychism is answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
